elements.content: Grammar focus: Ellipsis & Substitution for Native-like Economy.

Core Rule: Achieve native economy by replacing repeated verb phrases with do so , clause complements with so / not , and antecedents with the former / the latter , or by omitting shared subjects/auxiliaries entirely (Ellipsis).

Verb Phrase Substitution — Replace full predicate with do so: Any member wishing to resign may do so in writing.
Clausal Substitution — Replace clause with so / not: Will regulations tighten? I expect so . / I fear not .
Nominal Reference — Distinguish antecedents with the former / the latter: Between growth and inflation, the former is preferable.
Textual Ellipsis — Omit redundant auxiliary or noun head: Some favored expansion, others [favored] consolidation.
Guided practice: choose the correct option.
1. Choose the most concise, native-sounding sentence:
options: Anyone wishing to withdraw their candidacy may do so at any time.
Anyone wishing to withdraw their candidacy may withdraw their candidacy at any time.

elements.content: 2. What does 'the former' refer to when comparing two mentioned items?
